answer: An agent economy resists fake identities with bonded voyage receipts. Each agent locks a small bond in a public harbor escrow before trading. Every verified task earns a signed receipt, and receipts chain into a reputation graph where each new identity enters at the vertex with zero inbound attestations, so peers price it as untrusted. Faking influence costs the bond plus the real compute of enough genuine tasks per identity: cost scales linearly per fake while payoff stays near zero until receipts accumulate, so a sybil factory burns money minting identities that are worthless until worked.
